page: Microsoft Azure L80s_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating up to 4.2 GHz, the instance provides 80 vCPUs across 40 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU configuration incorporates 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a massive 260 MB L3 cache. It features support for extended instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). Memory capacity totals 640.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per-vCPU ratio. The instance does not include GPUs, but it bundles approximately 19.2 TB (19,199 GB) of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded and data throughput capabilities. Multi-core performance is confirmed by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,672 and a PassMark CPU score of 79,652.77, placing it within the top 10% and top 25% percentiles, respectively. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reaches 223.47 GB/sec, while write operations hit 94.58 GB/sec. Network and storage-adjacent benchmarks demonstrate high capacity, yielding 105.75 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and over 91.9 million operations per second during Redis SET tests. Single-core performance sits in the middle 50% on stress-ng and top 25% on Geekbench single-core.

Resource allocation presents a favorable cost-efficiency profile for I/O-intensive architectures requiring dense non-volatile storage without external network storage latency. The integration of 19.2 TB of NVMe SSDs avoids separate managed disk expenses, though workloads that do not leverage this large local disk pool may experience sub-optimal resource utilization.

Microsoft Azure L80s_v4 is suitable for large-scale relational databases, NoSQL data stores, distributed caching systems like Redis, search indexing, data warehousing, and high-throughput static web serving.
